label: copy-phase input g, late in the copy (recall_idx>=4), strongest when next output is g or q
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, almost exclusively when the fed-back input is g (98.6% of activation mass; a small remainder on input q). Never fires in the original or delimiter phase, and never at recall_idx <= 2. Within copy-phase g inputs, rate and magnitude rise with position: late steps (recall_idx >= 4, t >= 12, long sequences L=8-9) carry most of the mass. The strongest activations come when the token being output right after g is g (a gg pair) or q (a gq pair); out_tok g/q holds about 68% of the mass. Input g plus out_tok in {g,q} plus recall_idx >= 4 gives ~91% precision but only ~40% recall / 64% mass recall on dev. The rest are weak activations on late copy-phase g inputs followed by other tokens (l, p, 0, b, a with modest lift). Copy-phase g alone has ~97% recall but only ~6% precision, so most g inputs do not activate it.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: g, q, -, o, u, c; least: s, t, k, w) and the token being output (most: g, q, l, 0, a, p; least: k, -, j, v); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=5, t=15, recall_idx=4.
